name: Docs catalog to document

source.name: index.json
source.note: A catalog file conforming to old/documents.schema.json: { repo_version, updated, count, documents[] }. The mapper picks up documents[] automatically; the three wrapper fields are handled separately - see wrapper below.

rules.note: The old id is a kebab slug, not a UUID, so a new id is minted and the slug is preserved below.
The old kebab id keeps its meaning here - same value, correct field.
Old category is the folder name under docs/ (fema, military, technical-references, other). Already kebab, so it satisfies the new value pattern unchanged.
All four old values - active, superseded, deprecated, withdrawn - exist unchanged in the new enum, so this is an identity mapping.
date_added is a plain date; created_at is a date-time, so it becomes UTC midnight rather than drifting by the reader's offset.
Unlike the ATLAS import, the old kebab id is a genuine stable key, so re-imports are idempotent on (source_system, source_record_id).
path is required by the old schema, so every entry produces exactly one attachment.
This hashes the FILE, so it belongs on the attachment. The envelope's own checksum_sha256 hashes the record and is deliberately left unset.
Derived from the extension. An unrecognised extension yields no media_type at all rather than an invalid one - file_type still carries the raw value, so nothing is lost.
Deliberately NOT date-parsed. The target accepts YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD, and parsing a bare year to a full date would invent precision the publisher never stated.

NOT mapped to the envelope's superseded_by, which requires a UUID. The old value is a slug pointing at another entry whose new id does not exist until this run finishes. Parked here for a second pass - see followUp.

wrapper.note: The catalog's own three fields have no home on a record. Rebuild them with Preview > Download as collection, which emits { meta, items } per collection.schema.json.
wrapper.count: meta.count (recomputed from the output, not copied)

dropped.$schema: Points at the old catalog schema; the new file declares its own.

followUp: Resolve superseded_by. After the run, build a slug -> id index from the output, then for each record with metadata.superseded_by_slug set superseded_by to the matching UUID and delete the parked value. A slug with no match is a dangling reference in the source and should be reported, not silently dropped.
visibility is left unset so the schema default (internal) applies. If this catalog is public reference material, set it to public - as a constant rule here, not by hand afterwards.
url is unmapped: the old schema records a local path and an upstream source_url, but not a canonical web location for the document itself. Populate it where one exists.
Any row whose attachment has file_type but no media_type had an extension outside the lookup table. Add it to the table rather than leaving the field blank.
